claims.quote: But perhaps all elements are doing that at less perceptible rates.
claims.description: All chemical elements may be radioactive, decaying too slowly to detect.

claims.quote: If at a word, in one instant I could suddenly release that energy here and now it would blow us and everything about us to fragments
claims.description: Releasing a small lump of uranium's atomic energy all at once would make a devastating explosion, an atomic bomb.

claims.quote: if I could turn it into the machinery that lights this city, it could keep Edinburgh brightly lit for a week
claims.description: Atomic energy from a pint of uranium oxide fed into power machinery could light a whole city for a week.

claims.quote: Suppose presently we find it is possible to quicken that decay?
claims.description: Scientists find a way to speed up radioactive decay at will, releasing atomic energy on demand (induced radioactivity).

claims.quote: a source of power so potent that a man might carry in his hand the energy to light a city for a year, fight a fleet of battleships, or drive one of our giant liners across the Atlantic
claims.description: A hand-portable atomic power source able to light a city for a year, power warships, or drive an ocean liner across the Atlantic.

claims.quote: Every scrap of solid matter in the world would become an available reservoir of concentrated force.
claims.description: Any ordinary matter could be made to release its atomic energy as a fuel.

claims.quote: It would mean a change in human conditions that I can only compare to the discovery of fire, that first discovery that lifted man above the brute.
claims.description: Mastery of atomic energy would transform human life as profoundly as the discovery of fire.

claims.quote: We cannot pick that lock at present, but
claims.description: Humanity will learn to unlock the energy stored in atoms.

claims.quote: Then that perpetual struggle for existence, that perpetual struggle to live on the bare surplus of Nature’s energies will cease to be the lot of Man.
claims.description: Abundant atomic energy ends humanity's struggle for subsistence.

claims.quote: I see the desert continents transformed, the poles no longer wildernesses of ice, the whole world once more Eden.
claims.description: Atomic power is used to transform deserts and polar ice into habitable land, remaking the whole planet.

claims.quote: I see the power of man reach out among the stars
claims.description: Atomic power enables humanity to travel into space.

claims.quote: the problem of inducing radio-activity in the heavier elements and so tapping the internal energy of atoms, was solved by a wonderful combination of induction, intuition, and luck by Holsten so soon as the year 1933.
claims.description: A scientist achieves induced radioactivity in heavy elements, tapping atomic energy, in 1933.

claims.quote: What chiefly impressed the journalists of 1933 was the production of gold from bismuth and the realisation albeit upon unprofitable lines of the alchemist’s dreams
claims.description: Atomic disintegration transmutes bismuth into gold, though not profitably.

claims.quote: In the end, before many years are out, this must eventually change war, transit, lighting, building, and every sort of manufacture, even agriculture, every material human concern
claims.description: Atomic energy will transform warfare, transport, lighting, construction, manufacturing and agriculture.

claims.quote: some secret association of wise men should take care of his work and hand it on from generation to generation until the world was riper for its practical application
claims.description: A secret society of wise men withholds a dangerous discovery until humanity is ready for it.

claims.quote: Holsten, before he died, was destined to see atomic energy dominating every other source of power
claims.description: Atomic energy comes to dominate every other source of power within a lifetime.

claims.quote: It was in 1953 that the first Holsten-Roberts engine brought induced radio-activity into the sphere of industrial production, and its first general use was to replace the steam-engine in electrical generating stations.
claims.description: The first industrial atomic engine, introduced in 1953, replaces steam engines in electric power stations (nuclear power plants).

claims.quote: Hard upon the appearance of this came the Dass-Tata engine—the invention of two among the brilliant galaxy of Bengali inventors the modernisation of Indian thought was producing at this time—which was used chiefly for automobiles, aeroplanes, waterplanes, and such-like, mobile purposes.
claims.description: A compact atomic engine powers cars, aeroplanes and seaplanes.

claims.quote: the invention of two among the brilliant galaxy of Bengali inventors the modernisation of Indian thought was producing at this time
claims.description: A modernized India produces a wave of leading inventors who create key atomic technology.

claims.quote: Allowing for lubrication the Dass-Tata engine, once it was started cost a penny to run thirty-seven miles, and added only nine and quarter pounds to the weight of the carriage it drove.
claims.description: Atomic car engines weighing about nine pounds run thirty-seven miles for a penny.

claims.quote: by the autumn of 1954 a gigantic replacement of industrial methods and machinery was in progress all about the habitable globe
claims.description: Within a year of their introduction, atomic engines drive a worldwide replacement of industrial machinery.

claims.quote: For many years the price of coal and every form of liquid fuel had been clambering to levels that made even the revival of the draft horse seem a practicable possibility
claims.description: Coal and liquid fuel prices climb for years toward an energy crisis before atomic power arrives.

claims.quote: It made the heavy alcohol-driven automobile of the time ridiculous in appearance as well as preposterously costly.
claims.description: Before atomic engines, the standard automobile of the mid-twentieth century is a heavy alcohol-fueled car.

claims.quote: In three years the frightful armoured monsters that had hooted and smoked and thundered about the world for four awful decades were swept away to the dealers in old metal, and the highways thronged with light and clean and shimmering shapes of silvered steel.
claims.description: Within three years old fuel-burning cars are scrapped and roads fill with light, clean, quiet atomic vehicles.

claims.quote: men found themselves possessed of an instrument of flight that could hover or ascend or descend vertically and gently as well as rush wildly through the air
claims.description: Atomic-powered aircraft with helicopter lift that can hover and take off and land vertically as well as fly fast (VTOL aircraft).

claims.quote: in France alone in the year 1943 thirty thousand of these new aeroplanes were manufactured and licensed, and soared humming softly into the sky
claims.description: Mass private ownership of aircraft, with tens of thousands of new aeroplanes licensed in a single country in a year.

claims.quote: The railways paid enormous premiums for priority in the delivery of atomic traction engines
claims.description: Railways adopt atomic-powered locomotives.

claims.quote: atomic smelting was embarked upon so eagerly as to lead to a number of disastrous explosions due to inexperienced handling of the new power
claims.description: Industrial atomic smelting causes disastrous explosions through inexperienced handling.

claims.quote: the revolutionary cheapening of both materials and electricity made the entire reconstruction of domestic buildings a matter merely dependent upon a reorganisation of the methods of the builder and the house-furnisher
claims.description: Cheap atomic electricity and materials make rebuilding all housing feasible.

claims.quote: Patent-holding companies were presently paying dividends of five or six hundred per cent.
claims.description: Companies holding atomic-engine patents earn enormous profits.

claims.quote: this new supply of gold led quite naturally to a rise in prices throughout the world
claims.description: Gold produced as a waste product of atomic engines causes worldwide inflation.

claims.quote: The coal mines were manifestly doomed to closure at no very distant date, the vast amount of capital invested in oil was becoming unsaleable
claims.description: Atomic power makes coal mining and oil investments obsolete.

claims.quote: millions of coal miners, steel workers upon the old lines, vast swarms of unskilled or under-skilled labourers in innumerable occupations, were being flung out of employment by the superior efficiency of the new machinery
claims.description: Mass technological unemployment as millions of workers are displaced by efficient atomic machinery.

claims.quote: the rapid fall in the cost of transit was destroying high land values at every centre of population
claims.description: Cheap transport collapses urban land values.

claims.quote: gold was undergoing headlong depreciation, all the securities upon which the credit of the world rested were slipping and sliding, banks were tottering, the stock exchanges were scenes of feverish panic
claims.description: The atomic revolution brings a global financial crisis: gold loses value, banks totter and stock exchanges panic.

claims.quote: In the year 1955 the suicide rate for the United States of America quadrupled any previous record.
claims.description: The economic upheaval drives the US suicide rate to four times any previous record.

claims.quote: There was an enormous increase also in violent crime throughout the world.
claims.description: Worldwide violent crime surges amid the disruption caused by atomic energy.

claims.quote: The Dass-Tata people were indeed making a strenuous attempt to secure a world monopoly in atomic engineering.
claims.description: A company fights patent battles in court to win a worldwide monopoly on atomic engineering.

claims.quote: The world in these days was not really governed at all, in the sense in which government came to be understood in subsequent years.
claims.description: In later years government becomes a deliberate, planned design rather than a conservative contest among lawyers.
